institution: Thiruvananthapuram district AMR hub laboratory (General Hospital Thiruvananthapuram; spoke hospitals reported separately), KARS-Net district antibiogram, Department of Health Services, Kerala
citation: Kerala Antimicrobial Resistance Strategic Action Plan (KARSAP), Department of Health Services, Kerala. District Antibiogram: Alappuzha, Kottayam, Pathanamthitta, Thrissur and Thiruvananthapuram. Chapter: District Antibiogram, Thiruvananthapuram, January 2023 to December 2024, AMR Hub Lab, General Hospital Thiruvananthapuram, prepared by Dr Renuka M and Dr Ceena V Netto. Thiruvananthapuram: Department of Health Services, Kerala.
reporting: Percent resistant as typed labels on WHONET bar charts, by organism and specimen (pus, urine), hub laboratory isolates, all locations pooled; number tested not printed. Organisms with fewer than 30 isolates given as resistant/tested counts only.
method: WHONET (CLSI interpretation; references CLSI M39 5th ed. and M100 33rd and 34th ed.); cefoperazone-sulbactam read by EUCAST; colistin MIC and S. aureus vancomycin MIC not done.

verification.note: All resistance data are WHONET bar-chart images with percentage labels typed in the text layer. Each label was assigned to a bar by its x position (text layer) and checked on renders at scale 2.2 and scale 4; bar heights were then measured in pixels against the y axis (0 to 100, or 0 to 60 for Chart 4) and compared with the labels: they agree within about 2 points except where a conflict is recorded. Labels that sit between two bars, over duplicate breakpoint bars with different values, or that match no bar were left out (see excluded). Page numbers are 1-based PDF pages of the five-district compilation.

notes: District antibiogram of secondary and primary care facilities: rows are from the AMR hub laboratory at General Hospital Thiruvananthapuram (secondary care), 1 January 2023 to 31 December 2024 (two years), from the KARSAP compilation of five district antibiograms. The chapter prints a separate multihospital antibiogram for six spoke hospitals (General Hospital Neyyattinkara, Taluk hospitals Fort, Attingal and Varkala, W&C hospital Thycaud, DMH Peroorkada), which is not included (one row per stratum). All figures are percent resistant read from typed chart labels; the number tested per drug is not printed. Values whose drawn 95% interval spans more than 45 points (roughly a dozen or fewer isolates tested) were left out, as the report itself advises against percentages below 30 isolates.
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: the 40-cell seeded sample was read blind from the page images (scale 2.5, axis strips at scale 5), then all 84 cells and all 8 row n values were re-read and compared: 0 transcription errors; organism, specimen (pus, urine) and N correct on every row.

Label-to-bar check on every chart: the bar centres, y-axis ticks and bar heights were measured in pixels at scale 4 and each text-layer label matched to its bar (x-axis drug codes read on zoomed crops, including the two-row staggered codes); all 84 recorded labels sit on the bar of the recorded drug and agree with its height within about 1 point (at most 1.2 points, within the measuring error), apart from the three recorded label/bar conflicts.

Cautions confirmed as printed: Enterococcus urine erythromycin labelled 94% with the bar at 99.6% (Chart 5); E. coli pus amikacin labelled 35% with the bar at 37.1%, level with gentamicin (Chart 6); E. coli urine ciprofloxacin labelled 60% with the bar at 56.8% (Chart 7); Klebsiella pus cefotaxime 77% against ceftriaxone 50% (Chart 9, both labels match their bars).

Two excluded-entry reasons reworded for accuracy (no data change): the cefazolin labels can be matched to their bars, the ambiguity is which breakpoint set each bar uses; Chart 8 cefepime is drawn at about 31%, not 32%.
